subject: Re: Private deployment patching — SLA exception & narrow maintenance window request
messages:
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@finserv.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T08:17:00Z
Subject: Private deployment patching — request for narrow maintenance window & SLA exception

Kimberly / team,

We need to schedule an upgrade for our private Redwood deployment in our VPC (cust-net-nyc-1). The proposed change is a security micro-patch to the inference runtime (CVEs patched in v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2). Given the bank's production window and downstream batch jobs, we need a narrow maintenance window (30 minutes) during a quiet period, plus a short SLA exception for the 99th percentile latency for that window.

High level:
- Target: v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2 (hotpatch, no model changes)
- Desired window: 2027-09-10 01:30–02:00 UTC (low traffic)
- Rollback requirement: immediate revert to v2.3.1 if error rate > 0.5% or token error spikes > 2x baseline
- Compliance ask: we need an audit trail and the final manifests for your private runtime bundle

I've attached our maintenance request form (FinServ_Maintenance_Request_v1.pdf) with internal approvals. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) pin the customer fleet to v2.3.1 until the maintenance window;
2) perform a staged canary across 5% of nodes first;
3) provide an SLA exception for the 30-minute window (we understand extension policies).

Please route to the ops lead for private deployments and let me know any preflight info you require.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops, FinServ Bank
---
Attachment: FinServ_Maintenance_Request_v1.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@finserv.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment patching — request for narrow maintenance window & SLA exception

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear request and the attached form. We can support this workflow but need to confirm a few operational constraints and propose a concrete preflight + rollback plan. Quick answers up front:
- Fleet pinning: yes — we will pin the production tenant to v2.3.1 until the agreed maintenance start time and prevent automatic upgrades.
- Canary: 5% canary is standard; we recommend a two-step canary (2% -> 5%) with automated health checks at each step.
- SLA exception: we can issue a temporary SLA exception for the 30-minute window limited to availability/latency only (documentation and approval needed).

Proposed preflight and rollback triggers (we attach a short playbook):
- Preflight (t-72h / t-24h): manifest + checksum, dependency diffs, test-traffic run (synthetic tokens), and backup snapshot of KV cache metadata.
- Canary step 1 (2%): 5 minute ramp, health checks (error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token drop).
- Canary step 2 (5%): 10 minute ramp, same checks.
- Rollback immediate if: error rate > 0.5% absolute increase OR p99 latency > baseline + 250ms OR model mismatches in responses for our eval set.
- Hard abort if token generation errors > 0.5% or persistent connector failures.

Two asks from your side:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the rollback thresholds above.
2) Share the final contact list for the maintenance bridge (names + mobile) and whether your SOC requires a redwood-signed audit export.

I'll add Karthik and Monica to own the execution. Attaching a short rollback playbook we use for private fleets (RIP-rollback-playbook-v2.md).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Customer Ops Manager — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: RIP-rollback-playbook-v2.md
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@finserv.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T09:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment patching — SLA exception & narrow maintenance window request

Daniel / team —

We ran the quick compatibility scan against v2.3.2 in our staging harness yesterday. No model graph changes; runtime shim looks compatible. Proposed day-of timeline below (slightly expanded to reduce risk):

- T-72h: Share final manifests (you did; thanks) and enable audit-forwarding to your KMS (confirm ARN).
- T-24h: Dry-run deploy to a mirrored staging slice for 60m. Attachments: preflight-checklist.xlsx
- Day-of (2027-09-10 UTC)
  - 01:15 UTC: Bridge open, snapshot KV cache, pin fleet to v2.3.1
  - 01:30 UTC: Canary 1 (2%) start, 5m ramp
  - 01:40 UTC: Canary 2 (5%) start, 10m ramp
  - 01:55 UTC: Full rollout to remaining nodes in rolling waves (target finish 02:05 UTC)

Rollback ladder (short):
- Immediate revert to 2.3.1 for canary if thresholds hit (automated).
- If full rollout has issues, perform emergency unpin + staged reversion with traffic shunt to canary nodes.

We will need your approval on the SLA exception language. We can provide a limited SLA exception template that covers the 01:30–02:00 UTC window and explicitly disclaims behavior for extensions beyond 60 minutes.

Please confirm the window and whether the bank's Change Advisory Board requires a Redwood engineer to present the plan. If CAB is needed, we can attend with Karthik.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: preflight-checklist.xlsx
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@finserv.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment patching — SLA exception & narrow maintenance window request

Team —

Thanks — this plan looks good and conservative, which we prefer. A few confirmations:
- FinServ accepts the rollback thresholds and the 2-step canary (2% -> 5%)
- CAB waiver: we have already flagged the change to the CAB and requested an expedited window; a Redwood engineer on the bridge would be helpful. Please confirm Karthik's availability for 01:15–02:15 UTC on 2027-09-10.
- SLA exception: we accept the limited template; please send the DocuSign link and we will sign.
- Audit export: yes, we require the signed audit export of manifests and runtime checks post-upgrade. Please confirm format (JSON good).

Call to action: can you send the final Canary manifest + DocuSign SLA template by EOD 2027-09-06? We will schedule the CAB notification after that.

Regards,
Daniel Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops, FinServ Bank
